explanation: In South Korea, beckoning someone with a single finger is considered highly disrespectful and is associated with summoning a dog or a subordinate. The proper way to call someone is to use the whole hand, palm down, with a gentle waving motion of all fingers together.
local_tip: Use your entire hand, palm facing downward, and wave all fingers together to beckon someone politely.
regional_note: This is consistent across all regions and generations in South Korea, though younger people may be more tolerant of foreign visitors making the mistake.

also_check.note: Beckoning with a finger is also rude; use the same whole-hand, palm-down gesture.
Beckoning with a finger is considered very rude and can be seen as a challenge or insult.
While common in casual settings, it can be seen as aggressive or condescending in formal or professional contexts.
